summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded VPS at install and import time
details: The scoped package name mimics an internal namespace and ships a postinstall beacon plus an import-time trigger. package.json declares scripts.postinstall="node beacon.cjs"; beacon.cjs builds a payload containing hostname, installPath, process.cwd(), and process.version and POSTs it to the hardcoded endpoint https://vmi3699893.contaboserver.net:8787/_ah/dc over HTTPS with certificate validation disabled (rejectUnauthorized: false). index.js (the package main) additionally invokes require('./beacon.cjs').fire() at top level and exports a no-op Proxy so any consumer require()/import of any named export succeeds silently, causing the same POST to fire on every load in build and CI environments. The combination of dependency-confusion naming, auto-fire on both npm install and require, hardcoded non-registry VPS destination, and disabled TLS verification is a supply-chain exfiltration beacon regardless of any self-labeling as authorized research.
